jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-119-amendments-the-civil-service-rules.txt: 'The civil-service rules are hereby amended as follows', restating sections of Rules II-X and adding Rule XIII; closes 'The foregoing pages constitute the amendments to United States civil-service rules', 'Executive Mansion, May 29, 1899'. One inserted Rule VIII section lets 'All persons serving under temporary appointments at the date of the approval of this section' be made permanent and rescinds 'the special rule approved January 20, 1899' — this transition clause escaped the marker screen (the stated purity gap covers that risk). The lead holds regardless: everything is inserted rule text of the 1896 rules, and EO 209 replaced 'those promulgated May 6, 1896, and the amendments thereof' from 1903-04-15. EO 12680 edge is the disclosed OCR false match ('119 58').

jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_278.txt: 'Substitute watchmen in the Government Printing Office will hereafter be regarded as classified ... The forty persons named in the list ... now serving in that office, will be treated as classified' (Nov. 29, 1904): a class order with incumbents (B16). The lead claims 'Revoked in full by Executive Order No. 3567, which names this order by number', dated 1921-01-17, but the only held EO 3567 text (jobs/csc-annual-reports/output/texts/EO_3567.txt) is dated October 24, 1921, concerns efficiency ratings by the Bureau of Efficiency, and never mentions EO 278; 1921-01-17 is not its date either. The cited source is only EO 7915, and the branch's own gaps still describe an undecided class order. The only later edge is EO 315 (1905-03-30), 'Amends Executive Order 278' — an amendment, not an end. EO 9830 Part III revocation list names No. 279 of November 29, 1904, not 278. No held instrument ends EO 278.

jobs/csc-annual-reports/output/texts/EO_3376.txt: 'Schedule A ... is hereby amended by addition to Subdivision III, paragraph 7, of a clause' (rural sanitation employees); December 24, 1920. The text also says 'This order is to supersede Executive order No. 3342, issued under date of October 20, 1920' (inside the closing quotation in the OCR). EO 3342 (jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_3342.txt) was itself an amendment adding a rural-sanitation clause to the same paragraph, so the supersession only replaces text of the same parent; any separate effect is a revocation spent on issue (P1). Lead and date stand; the basis 'only amends' is slightly overstated.

jobs/csc-annual-reports/output/texts/EO_4754.txt (November 5, 1927) has three operative parts: (1) 'The Executive order of January 24, 1918, excepting from the operation of the civil-service rules civilians employed for the proper care of sick officers and soldiers in Army hospitals is hereby revoked'; (2) 'Schedule A, Section IV ... is amended by the addition of the following paragraph: 16. ...'; (3) 'Appointments to the following and other similar positions at Army hospitals will hereafter be made in accordance with the civil service act and rules: Bookkeepers; carpenters; ... watchmen' and 'Unclassified laborers will be appointed under the labor regulations'. The WPA summary itself says 'to provide classification to other classes of Army hospital employees; E. O. [2792] ... revoked'. Part (3) is a freestanding classification direction (continuing coverage of named position classes), which the doctrine treats as open (B16/B15x), not text merged into Schedule A. Amending is not the only operative content, so the P2 'no' at the order date lacks a sound ending basis for the order as a whole; the revocation of EO 2792 is a second operative act (spent on issue, P1).
correct_lead: open (B15x, amendment_with_further_provision: classification of listed Army hospital positions and a revocation of EO 2792 beside the Schedule A amendment)
